config.title: FUNDA — Auto-save Draft Widget

intro.title: FUNDA — Auto-save Draft Widget
intro.body: In this lesson you will build an Auto-save Draft Widget — a text editor form that silently saves the user's content to the server every time they pause typing, displaying a status indicator (Saving… → Saved ✓ → Error ✗) without an explicit save button. You will tap the FormControl's valueChanges stream, debounce it, and use concatMap to queue save requests so they never run out of order. The widget uses an optimistic UI pattern — local state updates immediately while the network call is in flight, rolling back on failure.
intro.usecase: Auto-save is a foundational feature of modern productivity tools — Google Docs, Notion, Confluence, and GitHub Issues. concatMap prevents out-of-order saves; mergeMap would fire parallel requests that could arrive out of order.

objectives: Subscribe to FormControl.valueChanges and apply debounceTime(800) and distinctUntilChanged() to throttle save triggers
Use concatMap to queue save HTTP requests so they execute sequentially and never overlap or arrive out of order
Manage a save status signal (idle / saving / saved / error) and display it as a floating badge that auto-clears after 3 seconds
Implement optimistic UI — update the local draft state immediately and roll back if the server returns an error
Initialise the editor with the latest draft from an API call on ngOnInit using the resolver or a direct HTTP call
Unsubscribe from valueChanges on destroy using takeUntilDestroyed(destroyRef) and explain why forgetting this causes a server spam leak
Contrast concatMap with mergeMap for this use case and demonstrate with a marble diagram why mergeMap would cause data corruption
